judgments.rationale: The activity-specific reading best fits the exact issue question, which asks whether activities performed by an RA 13 depositary in its capacity as a Transfer Agent are subject to the CMR. The answer’s phrase “only when such LC is not acting as a Transfer Agent” therefore plausibly evaluates the LC’s capacity in the handling under assessment. The formula correctly preserves the conjunctive RA13, scheme-money and Hong Kong conditions and negates only the Transfer Agent condition. The Schedule 11 passage supports treating other handling as subject to separate expectations rather than converting this predicate into a whole-law exemption. The wording “such LC” nevertheless leaves an entity-wide reading textually possible, so the interpretation is supported contextually rather than conclusively established.

source_evidence.quote: Would activities that an RA 13 depositary performs in its capacity as a Transfer Agent (TA) (eg, processing payments in designated accounts) be subject to requirements under the CMR?

The CMR will apply to an RA 13 licensed corporation (LC) and its associated entity (AE) in respect of “scheme money” received or held in Hong Kong by the RA 13 LC or its AE in the course of conducting Type 13 regulated activity by the RA 13 LC, only when such LC is not acting as a Transfer Agent.

In such cases, the depositary is expected to observe relevant requirements under Schedule 11 to the Code of Conduct for Persons Licensed by or Registered with the Securities and Futures Commission (Schedule 11), in particular paragraphs 9 (relating to how subscription and redemption proceeds should be held) and 11 (relating to distribution proceeds).

judgments.unresolved_question: Does “such LC is not acting as a Transfer Agent” refer to the LC’s capacity in the particular money-handling activity, or to any concurrent Transfer Agent activity of the LC generally, including unrelated funds?

judgments.rationale: This is the same activity-specific construction and is a defensible formalization of the selected applicability antecedent. It preserves “only when” as a condition on the coordinated LC-and-AE application statement and attaches “not” to acting as a Transfer Agent. The Q1 wording about activities performed in that capacity supports evaluating the role in the particular handling. The formula therefore captures a supported reading of the supplied text, while remaining limited to Q1 applicability and not whole-law compliance. As with the other activity-specific proposal, the source does not definitively exclude an entity-wide interpretation based on the phrase “such LC.”
